newsitem.title: USA: House Republicans attack U.S. role in Gaza talks.
newsitem.headline: House Republicans attack U.S. role in Gaza talks.

text.p: House of Representatives Republican leaders led by Speaker Newt Gingrich told President Bill Clinton on Thursday that U.S. participation in a Gaza conference sponsored by Palestinian Leader Yasser Arafat was a mistake.

The letter said that by agreeing to participate in the conference, Washington was sending a message that it was possible to drive a wedge between the United States and Israel, which is not invited to the conference.

"We believe the decision for the United States to participate this weekend in an international conference in Gaza sponsored by Yasser Arafat is a critical mistake and a slap in the face of a faithful ally," the 10 Republicans, including the top leadership, said in a letter to Clinton.
The State Department has called attendance at the conference "appropriate."

"This is an opportunity for the Palestinians to express their concerns about the present situation in the Middle East and to hear the views of friendly countries like the United States," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday.
Washington announced on Tuesday that the U.S. consul general in Jerusalem Edward Abington, would attend the gathering. The decision upset Israel.
The Republicans used the decision to criticise Clinton's policy more generally.

"Frankly, Mr President, we are deeply concerned with what we see as a pattern you and others in the administration have taken in recent weeks in publicly criticising Israel," the letter said. "Any disagreements we may have with our ally should be expressed privately. That is the way friends treat friends."
Clinton has criticised Iraeli building plans in the Jerusalem area.

The Republicans said they saw no reason for either public or private disgreements with Israel, declaring that "Israel should be receiving our praise for its sustained commitment to the peace process, particularly given the lack of reciprocity by the Palestinians."
